fields.v: Specification-driven governance framework (authors' own, unnamed), version Not stated. In the model studies: 'one-shot' spec-then-code, 'staged' spec then fresh-generation implementation, spec-first prompting, chain-of-thought and direct generation arms

Specification, high-level design (HLD) and low-level design (LLD), approved together as the auditable baseline (invariants/clauses); RACI responsibility matrix (Table I); audit trail: approved baseline with approver and timestamp, drift log (each divergence and violated invariant/clause), reconciliation record (code or document changed, by whom, why)

Five control points: (1) spec authoring (spec, HLD, LLD before code); (2) specification review gate (approve as baseline); (3) guided generation (model generates code from approved documents); (4) drift detection (code vs baseline); (5) reconciliation (human resolves each drift by correcting code or updating documents and re-approving the baseline)

Specification review gate modelled on HLD/LLD reviews (criteria: completeness, clear interfaces, explicit constraints, testable behaviour); drift review against the baseline; human reconciliation of every flagged drift; accountability always with a named human (Owner accountable, Table I)

Human and automated-reviewer studies: drift review step only (reviewing AI-generated code against an approved spec/HLD/LLD vs code only). Case study: full workflow (author walkthrough). Model studies: spec delivery modes (specification as separate artefact vs prompt text)

Not stated in Böckeler's terms; cites Piskala's spec-first to spec-as-source levels; framework treats the approved specification as source of truth and baseline kept in sync by reconciliation (closest to spec-anchored, classification by the drafter); long-term source-of-truth use is future work

Manual: reviewers record each drift, violated rule, location, start/end time and confidence; ground truth by adjudicating every distinct reviewer claim against the source code; paired Wilcoxon (human), Mann-Whitney (machine). Automatic: executable checker for model studies (validated with known correct and naive references)

Human study (criterion: adjudicated ground-truth drifts): (a) baseline-anchored review (spec+HLD+LLD) + human reviewers, n=5: recall 0.525, attribution 0.81, 5.6 drifts, 48.4 min, confidence 4.2. Quality: partly (attribution works, recall about half of verified drifts); cost: does not work (+21.7 min per review). (b) code-only review + human reviewers (comparison condition): recall 0.518, attribution 0.00, 5.4 drifts, 26.7 min, confidence 3.4. Quality: partly (recall about half, no attribution); cost: works. Automated-reviewer replication, 90 reviews by Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro (agent Not stated; per-model values Not stated): (c) baseline-anchored: recall 0.376, attribution 0.67. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. (d) code-only: recall 0.377, attribution 0.00. Quality: does not work (low recall, no attribution); cost: not measured. Model studies (models and agent Not stated): (e) staged spec then fresh generation + weak model: pass rate 45.0%, failed builds -50%. Quality: partly (n.s., n=4); cost: not measured. (f) one-shot spec+code + weak model: 23.8%. Quality: does not work; cost: not measured. (g) direct generation + weak model (baseline): 23.8%. Quality: does not work; cost: not measured. (h) spec-first + two strong assistants: e.g. 92%. Quality: works; cost: not measured. (i) chain-of-thought + two strong assistants: e.g. 95%. Quality: works; cost: not measured. (j) direct + two strong assistants (baseline): e.g. 59%. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. Case study: framework caught 2 issues at the review gate and 2 by drift detection; unconstrained run kept both defects (illustrative, author-conducted; no verdict)

rev.why: Incomplete: the form needs a quality and a cost verdict for every entry; (b), (d), (g), (j) had none and most entries lacked a cost verdict. (h) judged on its own (92%) is 'works', not 'partly'. Verdicts are judgements.

Cost verdict of (a) 'does not work' rests on the +21.7 min difference to code-only, i.e. a comparison, while the form asks for each configuration judged on its own (48.4 min per review could be 'partly'). Quality verdicts (c) partly vs (d) does not work at almost equal recall are also judgements. Values checked against Tables IV-V and Section V.

Values match Table IV, Table V and Section V. The verdicts are judgements: the cost verdict 'does not work' for (a) rests on the +21.7 min difference to code-only, but the form judges each configuration on its own (48.4 min per review could be 'partly'), and (c) partly vs (d) does not work at almost the same recall rests on attribution alone.

fields.v: Human study: within-subject, counterbalanced 2x2 (condition x service); 5 reviewers each did one review per condition; both services reviewed in each condition; no code execution, AI tools or web; baseline condition = code-only (public API only). Held constant: services, ground truth, attribution definition. Acceptance criterion: adjudicated ground truth (11 + 10 verified drifts), not the test suite. Repetitions: one review per reviewer per condition. Automated replication: same 2x2 design with 3 models, 90 reviews. Model studies: held-out scored criteria withheld from prompts; arms one-shot vs staged vs direct (n=4) and CoT vs spec-first vs direct over 10 function families and 2 assistants

Baseline-anchored vs code-only (human): recall 0.525 vs 0.518 (p=0.69, n.s.); attribution 0.81 vs 0.00 (p=0.043); time 48.4 vs 26.7 min (p=0.043); confidence 4.2 vs 3.4 (p=0.068); Fleiss' kappa 0.20-0.63. Machine: recall 0.376 vs 0.377 (p=0.95); attribution 0.67 vs 0.00 (p<10^-4), consistent across models. Model studies: staged 45.0% vs direct/one-shot 23.8% (p≈0.18, n=4, n.s.); spec-first vs CoT not significant (p≈0.28-0.32), CoT captures almost all spec-first gain

Distinguished conditions on attribution and time, not on recall. Repeatable: pattern reproduced by the automated replication. Limitations stated: n=5, signed-rank test floor p=0.043; confidence subjective; agreement on small groups; ground truth by adjudication because a test suite missed real drift; attribution measures traceability, not fix correctness; machine replication is convergent, not confirmatory; case study author-conducted; staged result has second-pass confound; model strength a dominant confound

Human study intentionally small (5 reviewers, 2 services, one domain); effects significant only for tested tasks; results 'preliminary and directional', 'strong pilot finding'. Framework adds upfront review cost; less value for short-lived or low-risk work; deployment difficulties: authoring discipline and spec-code synchronisation. Future work: spec as long-term source of truth after check-in, automated drift detection against LLD data contracts and state machines, LLM pre-screen (untested), larger human study with more reviewers, tasks and mid-strength models
